card.intuition: The task-relevant information the agent has access to right now. It is not the raw token input the model sees (that's the context window), nor the running history (that's the session), but what the agent knows that pertains to the task at hand.
card.analogy: A surgeon's prep table: at any moment only what's pertinent to the current operation is laid out. A table crowded with stale test results is worse than the single relevant fact placed front and center.
card.time_complexity: The model re-reads the entire context on every turn, so cost and latency grow with context size per request.
card.space_complexity: Context competes for space in the finite context window; task-relevant information must be loaded in while irrelevant content stays out.
when_to_use: Before judging an agent's output, ask what facts were in context when it acted
Loading the type definition or file a task turns on rather than letting the agent guess from call sites
Curating the context actively as part of an agent workflow
gotchas: Context is a measure of quality, not quantity — a nearly full window can still be poor context if it's full of stale tool output
Most day-to-day agent failures trace back to context: the relevant fact was never loaded, or was buried under attention degradation

steps.label: Task starts
steps.annotation: A new task begins; only known facts are in context.

steps.label: Load files
steps.annotation: The agent reads the definitions and files the task actually turns on.

steps.label: Curate
steps.annotation: Irrelevant or stale output is kept out so it cannot steer the agent.

steps.label: Act
steps.annotation: Each decision is made against the loaded, task-relevant facts.

steps.label: Reconcile
steps.annotation: When output misses, the first question is what was in context when it acted.

exercise.prompt: Check whether a required fact is present in the agent's loaded context files.
hints: Return as soon as any loaded document contains the fact.
The loop already returns False after the last document if nothing matched.
exercise.test_code:
files = ["the user id is 42", "password reset uses email tokens"]
assert fact_in_context(files, "user id is 42")
assert not fact_in_context(files, "credit card number")
print('PASS')
